quests.instruction: Copy the word 'morning' onto your line. It has two arches, an r, and ends with a tailed g.
quests.question: morning
quests.hint: m has two arches, then o and r. n and i are small, n again, and g drops below the line. Put the dot on i at the end.
quests.explanation: A seven-letter word with many arches. Count the arches in 'mo-r-n-i-n-g' and keep them even.
quests.funFact: Dew forms in the early morning when the air cools and water vapor turns into tiny drops.

quests.instruction: Now try 'evening'. Check that the two e's match.
quests.question: evening
quests.hint: e, v, e, n, i, n, g. Both e's are closed circles with a level bar. The tail of g goes below the baseline.
quests.explanation: Repeated letters need to look alike. Compare your two e's with each other.
quests.funFact: In the evening, the Sun seems to set in the west because the Earth spins toward the east.

quests.instruction: Next word: 'window'. It has two pointed w's with an arch in the middle.
quests.question: window
quests.hint: w, i, n, d, o, w. The two w's are the same width. d is the only tall letter.
quests.explanation: Starting and finishing with the same letter gives the word a balanced look. Keep the two w's twins.
quests.funFact: The word 'window' comes from an old Norse phrase meaning 'wind eye'.

quests.instruction: Write 'monkey' on the line. It begins with an arched m and ends with a tailed y.
quests.question: monkey
quests.hint: m has two arches, o and n are small, k is tall, e is small, and y has a tail. Write the whole word before going back for details.
quests.explanation: A tall k in the middle and a tail at the end. Plan the heights before you begin.
quests.funFact: Most monkeys have tails, but apes do not.

quests.instruction: Your next word is 'rabbit'. It has a tall b and a tall t, and a double b.
quests.question: rabbit
quests.hint: r and a are small, then two tall b's, i has a dot, t has a cross. Keep both b's the same height.
quests.explanation: Double letters should be identical. Check that both b's have the same size bump.
quests.funFact: A rabbit's front teeth never stop growing.

quests.instruction: Let's write 'turtle'. It has two t's and a tall l.
quests.question: turtle
quests.hint: t, u, r, t, l, e. Both t's are medium height, l is tall. Cross each t at the middle line.
quests.explanation: Crosses on both t's should be at the same height. Level crosses make the word look neat.
quests.funFact: A turtle's shell is part of its skeleton.

quests.instruction: Write the word 'elephant'. It has l, h and t, with a tall letter in each part.
quests.question: elephant
quests.hint: e, l, e, p, h, a, n, t. l and h are tall, p has a tail, t is medium. Keep the small letters even.
quests.explanation: An eight-letter word with tall letters, a tail and small letters. Think about the word as 'ele-phant'.
quests.funFact: An elephant's trunk works as a nose, a hand and a straw.

quests.instruction: Copy the word 'giraffe' onto your line. It has two f's and a tailed g.
quests.question: giraffe
quests.hint: g has a tail, i has a dot, r and a are small, and the two f's are tall with crossbars. Add both crosses and the dot after.
quests.explanation: Two f's in a row should be the same height. Cross both with one straight line if you like.
quests.funFact: A giraffe has seven neck bones, the same number as a human.

quests.instruction: Now try 'dolphin'. It has d, l, h, and a tail on p.
quests.question: dolphin
quests.hint: d, l and h are tall, o is small, p has a tail, i has a dot, n is small. Keep tall letters at the same height.
quests.explanation: Three tall letters and one tail. The tall ones should be parallel and the same height.
quests.funFact: Dolphins communicate with clicks and whistles.

quests.instruction: Next word: 'umbrella'. It has a tall b and a double l.
quests.question: umbrella
quests.hint: u, m, b, r, e, l, l, a. b, l, l are tall. Keep the two l's parallel and the same height.
quests.explanation: An eight-letter word with a mix of arches, circles and tall stems. Take it in two parts: 'um-brel-la'.
quests.funFact: The word 'umbrella' comes from the Latin word 'umbra', which means shade.

quests.instruction: Write 'computer' on the line. It has p with a tail and t with a cross.
quests.question: computer
quests.hint: c, o, m, p, u, t, e, r. p drops below the line, t has a cross. All the other letters are small.
quests.explanation: Mostly small letters, with a tail and a cross. Keep the m's arches even.
quests.funFact: The word 'computer' once meant a person whose job was to do calculations.

quests.instruction: Your next word is 'birthday'. It has b, h, d and a tail on y.
quests.question: birthday
quests.hint: b is tall, i has a dot, r is small, t is medium, h and d are tall, a is small, and y has a tail. Write all the letters first, then add the dot and cross.
quests.explanation: Eight letters and many details. Write all the letters first, then add the dot and cross.
quests.funFact: 'Happy Birthday to You' is one of the most widely sung songs in the world.

quests.instruction: Let's write 'notebook'. It is two words joined: note and book.
quests.question: notebook
quests.hint: n, o, t, e, b, o, o, k. Write 'note', then 'book' without a gap. The b and k are tall, and the three o's should match.
quests.explanation: A compound word is made by joining two words. Keep the same size and spacing in both parts.
quests.funFact: In Hindi, the word for a school exercise book, 'copy', is borrowed from English.

quests.instruction: Write the word 'butterfly'. It has many tall letters and a tail at the end.
quests.question: butterfly
quests.hint: b, f and l are tall, both t's are medium, and y has a tail. You can cross both t's with one line if you like.
quests.explanation: A nine-letter word with tall letters and a tail. Planning space across the line is important.
quests.funFact: Butterflies taste with their feet.

quests.instruction: Copy the word 'playground' onto your line. It has p, l, y and g, so lots of tails and tall letters.
quests.question: playground
quests.hint: p and y have tails, l is tall, g has a tail, d is tall. Plan the space for ten letters across the line.
quests.explanation: Ten letters in one word is a big step. If the line is full, make the letters a little narrower, not taller.
quests.funFact: In hopscotch, children draw numbered squares on the ground with chalk.

quests.instruction: Now try 'hill'. All of its tall letters should reach the same height.
quests.question: hill
quests.hint: h, i, l, l. h and both l's reach the top line. Draw the l's parallel to each other.
quests.explanation: Three tall letters in a row. Their tops should line up like a row of fence posts.
quests.funFact: A hill is a raised piece of land smaller than a mountain.

quests.instruction: Next word: 'lamp'. It has a tall l, and a p with a tail.
quests.question: lamp
quests.hint: l is tall, a and m are small, p has a tail below the line. Keep the small letters even.
quests.explanation: Tall at the start, a tail at the end. The middle letters connect the two.
quests.funFact: The first lamps burned animal fat in hollowed-out stones.

quests.instruction: Write 'kite' on the line. The tall k and the t have different heights.
quests.question: kite
quests.hint: k reaches the top line, i has a dot, t is medium, e is small. Put the dot on i and cross t at the end.
quests.explanation: k and t are different heights, and recognizing which is taller helps your handwriting look natural.
quests.funFact: People first flew kites in China more than two thousand years ago.

quests.instruction: Your next word is 'jump'. Both j and p drop below the baseline.
quests.question: jump
quests.hint: j has a hook and a dot, u and m are small, p has a straight tail. Keep both tails the same length.
quests.explanation: A descender at each end. Make the tails match and you will have a balanced word.
quests.funFact: Kangaroos can leap several meters in a single bound.

quests.instruction: Let's write 'puppy'. It has three tails: p, p and y.
quests.question: puppy
quests.hint: Three descenders. Write them all with the same length, and make sure the u is between them.
quests.explanation: Three tails in a five-letter word. Making them the same length is a good test of control.
quests.funFact: Puppies are born with their eyes and ears closed.

quests.instruction: Write the word 'gym'. The first two letters both have tails.
quests.question: gym
quests.hint: g has a tail, y has a tail, then m has two arches and sits on the line. Keep both tails the same length.
quests.explanation: A three-letter word with two tails. The m in the middle stays on the line.
quests.funFact: Gymnastics has been part of the modern Olympic Games since the very first ones in 1896.

quests.instruction: Copy the word 'ball' onto your line. It has a double l, and both l's are tall.
quests.question: ball
quests.hint: b is tall, a is small, and the two l's are tall and parallel. Make them identical.
quests.explanation: Double letters should be twins. Write the second l by looking at the first.
quests.funFact: A ball bounces because it is squashed and then springs back into shape.

quests.instruction: Now try 'grass'. It has a double s.
quests.question: grass
quests.hint: g has a tail, r and a are small, and the two s's are the same size. Keep every letter between the middle line and the baseline.
quests.explanation: Two s's next to each other should look like a matching pair, with the same curves.
quests.funFact: Grass keeps growing from its base, which is why it can be cut and still grow back.

quests.instruction: Next word: 'bubble'. It has a double b in the middle.
quests.question: bubble
quests.hint: Write b, u, then the double b, then l and e. Make every stem upright and every bump on the right.
quests.explanation: Three b's in one word is a lot of stems and bumps. Keep them all the same size.
quests.funFact: Soap bubbles show rainbow colors because light bounces off their thin skin.

quests.instruction: Write 'mini' on the line. All four letters are stems and arches: keep the gaps equal.
quests.question: mini
quests.hint: m has two arches, then i with a dot, n, then i with a dot. Check the gap between each stem is equal.
quests.explanation: Stem-heavy words show uneven spacing quickly. Equal gaps make the word look steady.
quests.funFact: 'Mini' is short for 'miniature', which means very small.

quests.instruction: Your next word is 'union'. It has stems, a cup and a circle in a row.
quests.question: union
quests.hint: u, n, i, o, n. The gaps between u, n and i should be equal. o is a round letter and needs a bit less space.
quests.explanation: Round letters need slightly less space beside them than straight letters do. Your eyes judge the space by area.
quests.funFact: The United Nations was founded in 1945 and now has 193 member countries.

quests.instruction: Let's write 'minimum'. It has many stems: aim for equal gaps.
quests.question: minimum
quests.hint: m, i, n, i, m, u, m. Seven letters, mostly stems and arches. Put dots on the i's last.
quests.explanation: The longer the word, the more important the spacing. Equal gaps keep the stems from looking jumbled.
quests.funFact: Minimum means the smallest amount; its opposite is maximum.

quests.instruction: Write the two words 'big dog'. Leave a space between them about as wide as the letter o.
quests.question: big dog
quests.hint: Write 'big', lift your pen, leave a gap the width of an o, and write 'dog'. Keep both words the same size.
quests.explanation: Spaces between words tell readers where one word ends. A gap about one o wide is just right.
quests.funFact: Spaces between words were introduced by Irish monks about thirteen hundred years ago.

quests.instruction: Write the words 'red hat', with a clear space between them.
quests.question: red hat
quests.hint: Write 'red', then pause and leave one o-sized gap before 'hat'. The tall h and d reach the same height.
quests.explanation: A gap that is too small makes words run together. Too large looks like a missing word.
quests.funFact: Red is one of the first color names most languages develop, after black and white.

quests.instruction: Write 'my cat'. It has two words and two different letter heights.
quests.question: my cat
quests.hint: Write 'my' with a tail on y, leave one o-sized gap, then 'cat' with a tall t. Keep the baseline level.
quests.explanation: Two short words, both on the same baseline. The tail of y goes below, the rest stays on the line.
quests.funFact: Cats purr when they are happy, and also sometimes when they are hurt or stressed.
